AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND AND AIM
AbstractText.content: We developed a suturing method with string and clips for a single-channel endoscope. The feasibility of string clip suturing method was evaluated in this prospective pilot study.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: This study involved consecutive 10 patients who underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for duodenal tumor. Polyester string is tied to the arm part of partially outthrusted clip. Clip and string can be passed through an instrument channel (3.2 mm) of a single-channel endoscope. The clip with string is placed at the distal edge of the large mucosal. Second clip is hooked on the string, and placed at the opposite side. Both clips can be gathered by pulling the free end of the string, and additional clips are placed to achieve complete closure. This method was compared with the prior 10 patients without mucosal closure after duodenal ESD.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Mean size of resected specimen was 39.1±12.4 mm. The success rate of string clip suturing method was 100% (10/10). The mean procedure time was 23.4±13.8 minutes. Perforation during ESD occurred in one patient, and was successfully closed by this method. None of treated patients developed serious adverse event after the procedure. Compared with the no-suture group, the length of stay was significantly shorter (p-value 0.038) CONCLUSION: String clip suturing method appears to be a safe and effective method in closure of large mucosal defects.
